It forces every implementing class to declare the same method again
It makes the interface directly instantiable with new
It creates a constructor that runs before every implementing class constructor
explanation: A default method supplies an implementation in an interface. Implementing classes inherit it and may override it, subject to conflict-resolution rules.
optionExplanations: Correct. A default method supplies an implementation in an interface. Implementing classes inherit it and may override it, subject to conflict-resolution rules.

question: What happens if a class inherits two unrelated interface default methods with the same signature and provides no override?

The two default methods are concatenated into one implementation
The class must resolve the conflict by overriding the method
explanation: A class inheriting conflicting unrelated defaults must resolve the conflict explicitly, typically by overriding the method and optionally calling a selected InterfaceName.super method.

The language does not depend on class-loading order to resolve source-level ambiguity.
Method bodies are never concatenated automatically.

hint: The implementing class must make the design choice explicit.

question: Which statement about finally is most accurate?

It executes only when no exception occurs in the try block
It executes only when a matching catch block returns normally
It is guaranteed to execute even after abrupt JVM or operating-system termination

optionExplanations: Correct. finally normally runs during control transfer out of try/catch, including exceptional paths. It is not guaranteed after process termination or severe runtime failure, and abrupt completion in finally can override earlier control flow.

question: Why should a method generally avoid returning from a finally block?
options: A return in finally always causes the JVM to deadlock
A return in finally automatically closes every object reachable from the method
A return in finally is illegal Java syntax in all circumstances
A return in finally can suppress a pending exception or replace a return value from try or catch
explanation: Abrupt completion of finally can override earlier completion of the try/catch statement. This can hide failures and make behaviour difficult to reason about.

The construct is legal, though discouraged.

question: What does the Enum.valueOf method require as its name argument?

The exact declared identifier of an enum constant, including matching case
A display label returned by the enum’s toString method in every case
The fully qualified class name of an unrelated Java type
explanation: Enum.valueOf looks up a constant using its exact declared name. The lookup is case-sensitive and throws IllegalArgumentException when no matching constant exists.
optionExplanations: The method is name-based, not ordinal-based.

question: What is a common benefit of using a method reference such as System.out::println?

It allows the method to accept any parameter type without compile-time checking

explanation: A method reference is concise syntax for a functional-interface implementation that delegates to an existing method. The target functional interface still constrains parameter and return types.

question: Which Map view provides key/value pairs suitable for iterating over both keys and values?
options: values(), which returns a Set of immutable key/value pairs

entrySet(), which returns a Set of Map.Entry key/value pairs

question: What is the usual complexity of contains on a HashSet when hash distribution is good?
options: Guaranteed logarithmic time, because HashSet is always implemented as a balanced tree
Expected constant time, because hashing narrows the search to a bucket
Guaranteed linear time, because every element must always be compared
Constant time in every possible case, regardless of collisions or hostile inputs
explanation: HashSet lookup is expected O(1) with good hash distribution. Heavy collisions can degrade performance, and modern implementations may treeify certain bins under conditions.
optionExplanations: HashSet is not simply a balanced tree implementation.
Correct. HashSet lookup is expected O(1) with good hash distribution. Heavy collisions can degrade performance, and modern implementations may treeify certain bins under conditions.
A hash set normally does not scan every element.
Expected constant time is not an unconditional worst-case guarantee.

question: What does Stream.distinct use to determine duplicate object elements in an ordinary object stream?
options: The number of times each element has been mapped in the pipeline
The elements’ toString output and lexicographic ordering
The elements’ memory addresses only, regardless of equals
The elements’ equals and hashCode contracts to identify equal values
explanation: For reference streams, distinct identifies duplicates according to Object equality semantics, which rely on equals and hashCode. Classes should implement those methods consistently.
optionExplanations: Mapping count is unrelated to value equality.

hint: Connect stream distinct to the equality contract used by hash-based collections.

question: Why can a stream not normally be reused after a terminal operation?
options: A terminal operation permanently locks the source collection against all future reads
A stream can be reused only if its source contains primitive values
A stream represents a one-use pipeline; after terminal evaluation it is consumed
The JVM deletes the source collection as soon as a stream completes
explanation: Streams are designed for one traversal. After a terminal operation, attempting to reuse the same stream generally causes IllegalStateException. A new stream can be created from the source if it supports it.
optionExplanations: A terminal stream operation does not lock or delete the source collection.
Primitive streams are also one-use.

Correct. Streams are designed for one traversal. After a terminal operation, attempting to reuse the same stream generally causes IllegalStateException. A new stream can be created from the source if it supports it.
The source collection remains available.
hint: Recreate a pipeline from the source rather than reusing a consumed stream.

question: What is the difference between LocalDateTime and ZonedDateTime?
options: ZonedDateTime includes zone rules and identifies a regional time context; LocalDateTime has no zone or offset
LocalDateTime is mutable while ZonedDateTime is immutable
LocalDateTime always stores UTC while ZonedDateTime stores local daylight time only
ZonedDateTime contains only a calendar date and no time of day
explanation: LocalDateTime contains local date and time fields without a zone or offset. ZonedDateTime includes a ZoneId and resolves the local date-time in that zone’s rules. Both are immutable.
optionExplanations: Correct. LocalDateTime contains local date and time fields without a zone or offset. ZonedDateTime includes a ZoneId and resolves the local date-time in that zone’s rules. Both are immutable.
Both types are immutable.

question: What does Thread.join() allow one thread to do?

Acquire the intrinsic monitor of every object used by another thread

join is not a general monitor-acquisition operation.
interrupt is a separate operation and normally affects one target thread.

question: What is the purpose of Thread.interrupt()?
options: It rolls back all changes made by the target thread since its last checkpoint
It pauses the target thread permanently until another thread calls start again
It forcibly terminates the target thread immediately at an arbitrary instruction

Java does not provide safe arbitrary forced termination through interrupt.

hint: Treat interruption as a signal that the task should respond to cooperatively.

question: What is the usual purpose of marking a worker thread as a daemon thread?
options: It prevents the thread from calling synchronized methods
It indicates a background service thread that does not by itself keep the JVM alive after all user threads finish
It guarantees that the thread is interrupted when it accesses shared state
It makes the thread execute at a higher operating-system priority than every user thread

question: What does Class.getSuperclass() return for a class directly extending Object?

question: What does Node.js’s event-driven, non-blocking I/O model aim to support?

question: What is a Spring bean scope?

question: What does declaring an instance field final guarantee?

question: What is binary numeric promotion used for?

To choose which overloaded method is called after the method body has run

question: Why can an expression involving byte values produce an int result?

The JVM cannot execute arithmetic on values smaller than 32 bits
All arithmetic expressions in Java are evaluated using double precision
Java promotes byte and short operands to int for many arithmetic operations

question: What is the result type of the expression 1 + 2L?

int, because the left operand appears first in the expression

question: Which statement about NaN comparisons in Java floating-point arithmetic is correct?

NaN can occur only when an integer division by zero is performed

The number of non-null elements currently stored in the array

question: What does String.isBlank() test?

Whether the string has exactly zero characters and nothing else

question: Why is repeated String concatenation in a large loop often less efficient than StringBuilder?

question: Which statement about constructor overloading is correct?

question: What does this() do when used as the first statement of a constructor?

question: Which order describes Java’s ordinary access modifiers from most restrictive to least restrictive?

question: Can Java constructors be overridden by a subclass?

question: Which method is not dynamically dispatched through an object reference in the same way as an overridden instance method?

question: What is the purpose of the @Override annotation?
options: To force the JVM to execute the method before every superclass method
